newsitem.title: USA: First Union says reshuffles muni groups.
newsitem.headline: First Union says reshuffles muni groups.

text.p: First Union Capital Markets Corp, a unit of First Union Corp, is reorganizing its public finance and municipal bond trading operations in several key states, the company's public finance chief said.

Sandy Curlett, managing director and head of public finance at First Union, told Reuters that the moves mean the company would no longer trade or underwrite Philadelphia or Pennsylvania debt out of its Philadelphia office.

"We have been winding down for the past year many of the activities on that desk anyway," Curlett said. "Instead, what we are going to be doing is put on the desk in Charlotte an underwriter, a person who is specializing and solely focused on the Philadelphia and Pennsylvania markets."

Curlett said current employees in Philadelphia would be candidates for the Charlotte job, but if they decided not to relocate, First Union would attempt to find them jobs in other areas of the company.
He said the moves will allow First Union to increase the capital it dedicates to Pennsylvania markets, since it can better handle risk from the central Charlotte location.

"First Union has in the past year been in the process of significantly strengthening its focus on the public sector and as part of that what we're doing in Philadelphia is really is a continuation of that strategy," he said.
Curlett said the moves also mean that two sales people in Philadelphia and three in Newark will all move to a new office in Summit, N.J. One trader will move from Newark to Summit.
On the investment banking side, four of the bank's five public finance bankers in Newark will go to Philadelphia, joining the three already there. The fifth Newark banker will move to Summit.
Curlett said First Union's goal is to eventually grow to the point where it can lead manage large state bond issues like Pennsylvania's recent general obligation offering.
The bank plans to have all of the personell moves complete by May 1, he said.
